clue.text: Men start off training in religious school with grand entrance

indicators.note: the men and the opening letter sit inside the word for religious

parts.note: PI is a crossword abbreviation for pious, so religious
OR, other ranks, is the military term for ordinary soldiers as against officers

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: a coed is a coeducational school, taking boys and girls

explanation.surface: Soldiers begin training at a church school that boasts an impressive front door.
explanation.walkthrough: Men here are other ranks, the army's term for non-officers, and a coed is an American-style mixed school; 'start off' takes the first letter of training.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a columned porch, the classic grand entrance, so a building having one is porticoed.

clue.text: One taking off from capital city on time, touring an excessive amount

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
touring means going round, so the city goes around the excessive amount

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
OD, overdose, is an excessive amount of a drug

explanation.surface: A traveller leaving the capital on schedule, after a tour that went on too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps the city round the overdose. Taking off reads as departing by air, but it means mimicking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off someone means imitating them for comic effect, which is what a parodist does.

clue.text: Challenger maintaining velocity during Earth's rotation

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so velocity is held inside
rotation turns the word round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: an earth is a fox's lair
V is the symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A contender keeping up speed while the planet spins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotation' turns LAIR into RIAL, and V goes inside. Earth is not the planet but a fox's den.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival is a competitor, one who challenges another for the same prize.

clue.text: Conman is one criminal who won't get off

parts.note: the roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: criminal, as in a criminal mess, says these letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A swindler is a lawbreaker who will not be acquitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Get off sounds like escaping conviction; here it is getting off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: An insomniac is someone who cannot sleep, one who won't drop off at night.

clue.text: Glacial deposit used to be in estuary, miles from the top

indicators.note: the past tense sits in the trimmed estuary word
in a down clue, the top is the start, so miles comes off the front

parts.note: an estuary is a river's mouth
was is the past of be

explanation.surface: Silt left by ice once lay in a river estuary, miles away from the upper reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the top' strips the opening letter, leaving OUTH, and 'in' puts the past tense inside that. Miles from the top reads as distance from a river's source.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwash is sand and gravel washed out of a glacier by its meltwater and laid down beyond it.

clue.text: No say about church making money in the past

indicators.note: about means the drama goes around church

parts.note: Noh, also spelt No, is a classical Japanese drama, so No is an example of drama

explanation.surface: Having no voice concerning the church's fund-raising, back then.
explanation.walkthrough: No say reads as having no voice; it is No (Japanese theatre), say, meaning an example of drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Set to pair up with Bishop for Mass

indicators.note: Bishop for Mass says one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: to match things is to pair them up
M is the physics symbol for mass
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Instructions for a priest: be paired with the bishop for the celebration of Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads Mass as a church service, but it is only the letter M, swapped for B.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group of things made or dealt with together, a set in that sense.

clue.text: Money that's blown by players

definitions.meaning: the ... section are the trumpets, horns and trombones that musicians blow

explanation.surface: Cash that gamblers or sportsmen squander.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is slang for cash, and also names wind instruments made of the metal.

clue.text: A measure of warmth not coming from ventilation cover maybe

parts.note: the opposite of from is to, so going to is not coming from
a grating is a grid that may cover a vent

explanation.surface: A grille over an air vent is no source of heat.
explanation.walkthrough: TO is read as the opposite of 'from'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tog rating grades the thermal insulation of a duvet or garment, so it measures warmth.

clue.text: Set foot in lush forest

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom, the final letter

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Stepping into a green and leafy wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot in' takes H, the last letter of lush. Arden is an English forest in Warwickshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to become firm or solid, as jelly or concrete hardens.

clue.text: Goes over the top in jet, finally changing direction

indicators.note: the last letter is a compass point, and north turns to south

parts.note: jet black and raven black are both words for a glossy black, so jet can be raven

explanation.surface: A pilot overdoes the flying in a jet aircraft, at last turning round.
explanation.walkthrough: Jet looks like an aircraft but is the colour; 'finally changing direction' turns the closing N (north) into S (south).
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk or praise wildly, which is going over the top.

clue.text: Cape of old cloth lieutenant keeping at a distance returned

indicators.note: returned means the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a piece of old cloth

indicators.note: the lieutenant holds the distance word inside it

parts.note: afar means at a distance

explanation.surface: A cloak made of worn fabric, which a junior officer had kept far off, came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' makes LAFART; 'returned' turns the whole string round. Cape looks like a garment but is the headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Trafalgar is the headland in south-west Spain off which Nelson's famous 1805 battle was fought.

clue.text: Female on the cover to the left is a great poser

indicators.note: in an across clue, the woman being on the cover means she is written after it
in an across clue, going to the left means the word runs backwards

parts.note: a lid is the cover of a box or pot
Emma is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman posing on a magazine cover, facing left, is a great model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the left' turns LID into DIL. The surface makes a poser someone who poses; here it is a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question, and a dilemma, a choice between two bad options, is a hard one.

clue.text: Security label placed inside socks, say

indicators.note: the label is put within the word for socks

parts.note: hose is a word for stockings and socks, which are examples of it
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A security tag has been sewn into a pair of socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held as security, a pledge that terms will be kept.

clue.text: Seeing sense about drawing back, a girl is honest

indicators.note: the sense word goes about, or around, the drawing

parts.note: sight is the sense of seeing

indicators.note: back means the drawing word is read backwards

parts.note: drawing is art
Sadie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone coming to their senses after withdrawing says that a girl is honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives TRA and 'about' puts it in the sense word; the girl's name Sadie, after A, supplies the last two words of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight as a die is an idiom for completely honest, from the die's true, square faces.

clue.text: Leading statesman in war is potential vote-loser

indicators.note: potential suggests the letters are only one form they might take, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wartime leader is something that could cost a party at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: Franklin D Roosevelt was US president through most of the Second World War.

clue.text: Flattering article in different shades of blue, overlapping

indicators.note: the article goes in among the two blues

parts.note: blue can mean adult, as in a blue film
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the two words share the letter where they meet, so it is written once

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory is a blue

explanation.surface: A complimentary piece of writing on how several blues merge into one another.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue means both risqué and Conservative; 'overlapping' lets the two words share their T, giving ADULTORY, and 'in' puts the article inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulatory means expressing excessive admiration or praise, as flattery does.

clue.text: My clothes upset cardinal from Swiss city

indicators.note: clothes is a verb, the exclamation dressing the number

parts.note: gee and my are both mild exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the number upside down

parts.note: seven is a cardinal number

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that their clothes have offended a churchman from Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SEVEN into NEVES, and GEE clothes it. Cardinal looks like a churchman but is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevese is an adjective for people or things belonging to Geneva.

clue.text: Conjecture glen, strangely, is one far from beauty spot

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the two words are set out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Guesswork about a Scottish valley, oddly, suggests it is nowhere near pretty.
explanation.walkthrough: A glen sounds like a beauty spot itself, steering the solver away from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A concrete jungle is a grim built-up urban area, the opposite of a scenic beauty spot.

clue.text: Found fame with fur sort of pad

indicators.note: to found metal is to melt and cast it, reshaping these letters

explanation.surface: Someone won celebrity with a kind of furry cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: Found looks like a past tense; it is the verb for casting metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An earmuff is a padded covering, usually furry, worn over the ear against cold.

clue.text: Around start of afternoon you brought up jug and glasses

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read upwards

parts.note: ye is old-fashioned you

indicators.note: the jug goes around the opening letter

parts.note: a ewer is a large water jug

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' gives EY; 'Around' has the jug enclose the first letter that 'start of' picks. Glasses looks like tumblers to go with the jug.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewear is a collective word for spectacles and similar items worn over the eyes.

clue.text: Stop for a drink

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to put an end to it

explanation.surface: Calling in somewhere for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch means to put a stop to something, and is also whisky made in Scotland.

clue.text: Endless doubt associated with revolutionary design

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question

explanation.definitionFit: A chequer is a pattern of squares in alternating colours, a kind of design.

clue.text: Produce bubbly and aim to get tip

parts.note: a fizzy drink is said to be up when it froths and bubbles
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, to tip it over.

clue.text: One rescued after holiday in Brussels ends in complete nightmare

indicators.note: the holiday word goes inside the Brussels abbreviation

parts.note: EU, the European Union, has its headquarters in Brussels

clue.text: Organs reproducing every second of cult refrain

clue.text: Air show may start with police force — French one

clue.text: Backing incomplete survey exonerating member of Daisy's family

clue.text: Over fifty, unsettled, and single
